label: mean-age-2
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length California nontrawl fleet is available from 1978 to 1988, and in 2005. Mean age varried widely from 5 to 25 years old. Limited years of data were available.

label: mean-age-3
alt_text: The California recreational fleet had very sporatic conditional ages avialable, some were available for the early 1980s, 1995, and early 2010's. Overall, mean age ranged from 10-50 years old. Limited years of data were available.

label: mean-age-4
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length Oregon/Wasington trawl fleet is available from 2000 to 2024. Mean age varried widely from 2000 to 2011 around 5 to 40 years old. Then, from 2012 to 2024, mean age varried closer to 10-20 years old with less variance.

label: mean-age-5
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length Oregon/Wasington nontrawl fleet is available from 2001 to 2024. Mean age varried consistently around 25 years old, but with wide error bars around 2011, 2014, and 2020. Also, data was missing for 2016.

label: mean-age-6
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length Oregon/Wasington recreational fleet is available from 1980 to 2016, with very sparce data from 1980 to 2009. Mean age before 2009 ranged from 15-30 years. From 2009-2016 mean age varried from 5 to 25, with very wide error bars.

label: mean-age-7
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length Wasington recreational fleet is available from 1998 to 2024, with few years of missing data. Mean age varries between 10 and 35 years old. In 2010, mean age jumps to around 50 years old with high varriance.

label: mean-age-11
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length WCGBTS survey is available from 2003 to 2024, with data missing in 2020. Mean age varries between 20 and 25 years old until 2015, where the mean age drops to 15-20.

label: mean-age-12
alt_text: Mean age for the conditional age-at-length IPHC survey is available from 2001 to 2024, with data missing in 2020 and 2021. Mean age varries between 30 and 40 years old. However, the model expectation line consistently under estimates mean age across years, potentially due to high varriance in 2016 data.

label: spout_combined
alt_text: The combined area spawning output is relatively unfished between the start of the model until the mid 1950s with spawnign output sharply decreasing to low levels by 2000 remaining low until the early 2000s where spawning output begins to increase and reaches the management target of 0.40 by 2024.

label: spout_area
alt_text: Spawning output is relatively unfished between the start of the model until the mid 1950s with spawning output sharply decreasing to low levels by 2000 remaining low until the early 2000s where the spawnig output begins to increase and reaches the management target of 0.40 by 2024. The two areas generally follow the same trend, with Area 1 (California) consistently having a much lower spawning output compared to Area 2 (Oregon and Washington)

label: status_combined
alt_text: The combined area stock status is relatively unfished between the start of the model until the mid 1950s with the stock sharply decreasing to low levels by 2000 remaining low until the early 2000s where the stock begins to increase and reaches the management target of 0.40 by 2024.

label: status_area
alt_text: Stock status is relatively unfished between the start of the model until the mid 1950s with the stock sharply decreasing to low levels by 2000 remaining low until the early 2000s where the stock begins to increase and reaches the management target of 0.40 by 2024. The two areas generally follow the same trend, with Area 1 (California) consistently having a much lower relative stock status compared to Area 2 (Oregon and Washington)

label: totalbio
alt_text: Total biomass in metric tons by area is relatively unfished between the start of the model through 1950 with the biomass sharply decreasing to low levels by the mid 1990s remaining low, increasing in the early 2000s and to the end of the time series. The two areas generally follow the same trend, with Area 1 (California) consistently having a much lower biomass compared to Area 2 (Oregon and Washington).

label: summbio
alt_text: Summary biomass in metric tons by area is relatively unfished between the start of the model through 1950 with the biomass sharply decreasing to low levels by the mid 1990s remaining low, increasing in the early 2000s and to the end of the time series. The two areas generally follow the same trend, with Area 1 (California) consistently having a much lower summary biomass compared to Area 2 (Oregon and Washington).

label: tsrecuits
alt_text: Figure shows the total Age-0 recruites for the current base model. Recruitment generally peaked in the 1950s, 1970s, 1980s, and 2010s.

label: bridge25-comp4
alt_text: Figure comparing the fraction of unfished biomass trajectories for the 2017 and current base models. There is little to no difference between the two time series, and the time series from the current model seems to continue on the same general path that 2017 ended.

label: bridge25-comp12
alt_text: Figure compares the recriutment deviations between the 2017 assessment model and current base model. Recruitment generally peaked in the 1950s, 1970s, 1980s, and 2010s. The recent period (2010-2024) showed higher recriutment in the current model compared to the 2017 model.

label: full-jitter
alt_text: A jitter point plot showing the change in negative log-likelihood of 100 iterations. The majority of iterations fell in line with the base model likelihood (green dots), some (the blue dots) had higher likelihood, but none had a lower likelihood.

label: sens_model_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawning output between sensitivity models and the base model when estimating natural mortality, steepness, and using the 2017 length-weight relationship. There is a significant increase in spawning output when the model estimates either natural mortality or steepness.

label: sens_model_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model when estimating natural mortality, steepness, and using the 2017 length-weight relationship. There is a significant increase in stock status when the model estimates either natural mortality or steepness.

label: sens_lengths1_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawning output between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing few changes as length data are excluded.

label: sens_lengths2_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawnig output between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing no changes as length data are excluded. Except, when removing all length data, the spawning output nearly doubles.

label: sens_lengths1_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing no changes as length data are excluded.

label: sens_lengths2_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing no changes as length data are excluded. Except, when removing all length data, the status greatly increases.

label: sens_age1_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawning output between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing few changes as more age data are excluded.

label: sens_age2_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawning output between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing few changes as more age data are excluded. Removing the IPHC age data slightly reduced spawning output, whereas using the McAllister and Ianelli weighting increased the spawning output.

label: sens_age1_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing few changes as more age data are excluded.

label: sens_age2_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing few changes as more age data are excluded. Removing the IPHC age data slightly reduced overall fraction unfished, whereas using the McAllister and Ianelli weighting increased the fraction of unfished biomass.

label: sens_indices_spout
alt_text: Figure comparing spawning output between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing relatively little changes when removing indices with the exception of excluding all indices and the IPHC index.

label: sens_indices_status
alt_text: Figure comparing fraction of unfished biomass between sensitivity models and the base model, and showing relatively little changes when removing indices with the exception of excluding all indices and the IPHC index.

label: sens_sum
alt_text: A summary of the relative changes in management quantities from all sensitivity models with relative change on the x-axis and each data source removed on the y-axis. Plot highlights that the model is most sensitive to removing all length composition data.

label: sens_sum_no_lengths
alt_text: A summary of the relative changes in management quantities from all sensitivity models, except the removal of all length compostion data with relative change on the x-axis and each data source removed on the y-axis. Plot highlights that besides removing all length composition data, the model is most sensitive to estimating steepness and natural mortality.

label: retro-sp-output
alt_text: Plot of spawning output with uncertainty intervals over time. As years of data are removed there is no change to overall spawning output.

label: retro-rel-biomass
alt_text: Plot of relative biomass with uncertainty intervals over time. As years of data are removed there is no change to overall fraction of unfished biomass.

label: retro-recruit-dev
alt_text: Plot of recruitment deviations with uncertainty intervals over time. As years of data are removed there is little change to overall recuritment deviations.

label: status_assmnts
alt_text: Time series line plot with years on the x-axis and relative depletion on the y-axis.  Each line shows the change in the base model from the 2001 assessment to the current assessment. Overtime models have remained relatively consistent

label: natm-piner
alt_text: Four panel plot with natural mortality values on the x-axis and change in log-likelihood on the y-axis with panels showing the contribution from each data type in the model. The recruitment, recreational length data, and survey indices are the primarily source of information informing the estimate of natural mortality. There is little information about natural mortality from the age data.

label: natm-bratio
alt_text: Time series line plot with year on the x-axis and fraction unfished on the y-axis. The lines represent multiple model runs that assume a range of natural mortality values from 0.030 to 0.060. Any model with a natural mortality less than 0.044 has the fraction of unfished biomass fall below the management target of 0.40.

label: steep-piner
alt_text: Four panel plot with steepness values on the x-axis and change in log-likelihood on the y-axis with panels showing the contribution from each data type in the model. The recruitment and length data are the primarily sources of information informing the estimate of steepness. There is some information about steepness from the survey indices, but little from the age data.

label: steep-bratio
alt_text: Time series line plot with year on the x-axis and fraction unfished on the y-axis. The lines represent  multiple model runs that assume a range of steepness values from 0.25 to  1.00. Any model with a steepness less than 0.7 has the fraction of unfished biomass fall below the management target of 0.40.

label: rzero-piner
alt_text: Four panel plot with ln(R0) on the x-axis and change in log-likelihood on the y-axis with panels showing the contribution from each data type in the model. The recruitment data is the primarily source of information informing the estimate of log(R0) with index data  supporting higher log(R0). There is little information about log(R0) from the length and age compostion data.

label: rzero-sp-output
alt_text: Time series line plot with year on the x-axis and spawning output on the y-axis. The lines represent  multiple model runs that assume a range of ln(R0) values from 5.0 to 6.0. The lines are stacked with ln(R0) values of 6.0 with the highest spawning output, and ln(R0) of 5.0 with the lowest spawning output.

label: rzero-parm
alt_text: Four panel plot with ln(R0) on the x-axis and values on the y-axis as described in the caption. The likelihood figure reflects a bowl, with the minimum at the estimate of ln(R0). In the other panels, as ln(R0) increases, the spawning output relative to unfished, initial spawning output, and final spawning output all increase as well.

label: time-spr
alt_text: Time series plot showing fishing intensity above the SPR target of 50 percent in many years from 1900 to 1975, then a steep drop below SPR 50% until 2002, and again rises above 50% from 2002 to 2024.

label: eq-yield
alt_text: Yield curve shows equilibrium yield as a domed function of fraction of unfished spawning output, with a peak slightly below 0.3, a maximum sustainable yield around 120t, and a biomass target at 0.4.
